instruction: I'm starting a data analysis project using pandas. Please assist me in setting up the pandas library in /home/user and confirm that the DataFrame class can be imported correctly.

metadata.explanation: Task requires setting up pandas library and verifying DataFrame can be imported without errors. Similar complexity to original task - package installation and import verification. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_error getter to verify no import errors.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_vm_command_error executes 'python -c "from pandas import DataFrame;"' and returns stderr output, which will be empty on success or contain error messages on failure
Metric logic is correct: check_include_exclude with include=[] and exclude=['Error:'] correctly verifies no import errors occurred (returns 1.0 when 'Error:' not in result)
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies both requirements - pandas installation and DataFrame import capability - through a single import test
Expected value is semantically correct: Python import errors contain 'Error:' substring (e.g., ModuleNotFoundError:, ImportError:), so excluding 'Error:' correctly identifies successful imports
Edge cases handled: Empty stderr (success) returns 1.0, error messages (failure) return 0.0
No state dependencies: VM command execution is always accessible, no UI or postconfig needed
Verification adequacy: The import test is the standard and most reliable way to verify library installation and class availability
